## Charge in the cheapest quarter hours before a deadline

A new blueprint for an EV or a home battery. Plug in, or switch a "ready"
helper on, and it charges in the cheapest quarter hours left before the time
you set - say 07:00 - in as many pieces as the prices have valleys. Thanks
to Lars for the question that showed what was missing.

- **It decides again every quarter hour.** Come home at 17:00 after the
  cheapest hour at 13:00 has passed, and it takes the cheap hours of the
  night instead. Prices published after you plugged in are used as soon as
  they arrive.
- **Several valleys.** Two hours to charge and two cheap stretches at 00:00
  and 04:00? It charges in both and stops in between.
- **One automation per car or battery**, each with its own charging time and
  deadline: the car fills up at the bottom of the valley, the battery that
  needs three hours starts a little earlier.
- **The charging time can come from a sensor**, for example one worked out
  from the state of charge and your PV forecast, so the grid only covers what
  the sun will not.
- **With "Current retail price" as the price series**, time-of-day grid
  charges such as Germany's Modul 3 decide the valleys too.

If there is not enough time or data before the deadline, it charges straight
away. It switches whatever you choose - a wallbox switch, a charge-mode
select or the maker's action.

[![Import the blueprint](https://my.home-assistant.io/badges/blueprint_import.svg)](https://my.home-assistant.io/redirect/blueprint_import/?blueprint_url=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2FBackupBaTTerY%2Fenergypriceforecast-home-assistant%2Fblob%2Fmain%2Fblueprints%2Fautomation%2Fenergypriceforecast%2Fcharge_cheapest_before_deadline.yaml)

**After updating, restart Home Assistant.** The integration itself is
unchanged; the version marks the new blueprint.

## How do you use it?

A line in
[Discussions](https://github.com/BackupBaTTerY/energypriceforecast-home-assistant/discussions)
on what you charge and when decides what comes next.
